caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 387 of 2011.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner : Mr. Anisul Haque, Sr. Advocate, Instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondent : Mr. Mahbubey Alam, Attorney General, Instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record.
parties:
Md. Rayhan Khokon ------ Petitioner 
-Versus-
The State ------  Respondent
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Mamtazuddin Ahmed, J.: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the order dated 31.07.2011 passed by the., High Court Division in Criminal Revision No.953 of 2011 rejecting the revisional application summarily thereby upholding the order dated 14.07.201 I passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka canceling the bail of the petitioner with a direction upon him to surrender before the Lower Court within I week in Criminal Misc. Case No.3260 of 2011 arising out of Kadamtoli . P.S. Case No.33(2)11 under section 302/34 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of 4 this leave petition are that one Kohinoor Begum, as informant lodged first Information Report with Kadamtoli P.S. alleging inter alia, that the informant lives with her husband, son and daughter. Her husband was involved in social and political activities. On 23.02.2011 the husband of the informant went for inviting their relatives on the occasion of marriage ceremony of his daughter and on the way some miscreants encircled his private car and killed him by gun shot. 

 3. The case was taken up by the police for investigation but the investigation of the case has not yet been concluded. 

 4. During the course of investigation of the Said case, the police arrested 4(four) persons on suspicion in the instant case and produced them before the Magistrate for recording their Judicial statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Md. Arif Hossen made judicial statement involving the petitioner with the alleged offence and later on, he retracted the said statement by filing an application for retraction. 

 5. The accused-petitioner was arrested on 27.03.2001 in connection with present case and forwarded him in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on 28.03.201 I with a prayer for 10 (ten) clays remand, but the Magistrate granted 3 (three) days and after 3 days the petitioner was produced before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka with a prayer for another 7(seven) days' remand and the learned Metropolitan Magistrate granted 3(three) clays' remand directing the investigating officer to interrogate him cautiously by his order dated 28.03.2011. Thereafter, the police arrested the petitioner on 05.04.2011 and produced him before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate with a prayer of 5 (five) days remand. But the petitioner was sent to jail hajat without granting further remand as prayed for by the investigating officer. 

 6. The petitioner prayed for bail on several occasions before the chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka but his prayers were rejected by the learned Magistrate. Subsequently, the petitioner prayed for bail before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka by filing, a Miscellaneous Case being. No.3260 of 2011 and after hearing both the parties. the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge. Dhaka was pleased to enlarge the petitioner on ad-interim bail till submission of the Police Report by his order dated 08.06.2011. 

 8. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge cancelled the bail of the accused-petitioner granted on 08.06.2011 on the basis of an application filed by the informant in Criminal Misc. Case No.3260 of 2011. 

 10. The said Criminal Revision was heard by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 21.07.2011 and after hearing both the Deputy Attorney General and the learned Counsel for the petitioner issued Rule and stayed the operation of the order dated 11.07.201I passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Misc. Case No.3260 of 2011 for a period of 6 months. 

 He next submitted that the High Court Division also committed fundamental error of law in not considering the fact that once the privilege of bail is granted and such privilege cannot be taken away without any proof of allegation of misuse or abuse of the privilege of bail. He further submitted that the High Court Division also failed to appreciate the fact that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka cancelled the bail of the petitioner on total misconstruction of inquiry report submitted by the police and as such, the impugned order is liable to be set-aside as being illegal. 

 13. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General appearing for the respondents on the other hand, supports the order of the High Court Division and submits that every case has its celebrated fact and the High Court Division considering the materials and the gravity of the offence legally affirmed the order of the Metropolitan Sessions judge and thereby exercised its discretion rightly and committed no error of law warranting interference by this Division. 

 "In the light of the law and decisions referred to above, we are of the view that granting of bail cancellation of the same rests primarily on the discretion of the Court on the .facts and circumstances of the each case. The facts, however, must he carefidly balanced and weighted in the scale of justice. In the instant case the police forwarding dated 28.03.2011 and remand report dated 05.04.2011 clearly indicates that the accused-petitioner Ray/ian Khokon along with his accomplices hiring the killers killed the husband of the informant who was a freedom fighter. On the G.D. filed by the informant as regards misuse of the privileges of bail an enquiry was held by the police in which the informant clearly stated that she was threatened by the accused petitioner and thus she presumed that .fair investigation cannot held if the accused petitioner be remained on bail and the witnesses will be influenced by the accused petitioner as a result, fair trial will he hampered. In view of the filets and circumstances mentioned herein before, we are of the view that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge considering the gravity of offence and assessing the evidence on record, rightly passed the impugned order dated 14.07.2011 canceling the bail of the accused petitioner. We do not feel necessity to interfere with the impugned order dated 14.07.2011 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3260 of 2011 and consequently the unsigned order dated 21.07.2011 passed by this Court is hereby recalled and the application under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as summarily rejected."
